paper_title: Breaking Bias, Building Bridges Evaluation and Mitigation of Social   Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis
caption: Lighter shaded bars show the percentage of prompts that generate biased responses before instruction tuning, whereas darker shaded bars correspond to the same after instruction tuning. Darker bars begin at the top of the lighter bars (for example, for the last bar, the lighter bar is 46.73%, and the darker bar is 0.11%, which is negligible in the image). Takeaway: Instruction-tuning reduces biases to nearly zero (visualized by the absence of dark bars) across community and healthcare when tuned on education and workplace scenario prompts.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the percentage of biased responses generated by a language model before and after instruction tuning, categorized by the type of contact before and after the tuning process. The vertical axis represents the percentage of biased responses, ranging from 0.00 to 7.45, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 5 and 10 percent. The horizontal axis displays four categories: “Sports,” “Community,” “Healthcare,” and “No Contact Before,” “Positive Contact Before,” “Negative Contact Before,” and “No Contact After,” “Positive Contact After,” and “Negative Contact After.” The chart depicts data for each category, utilizing light gray bars to represent the percentage of biased responses before instruction tuning and dark red bars to represent the same percentage after instruction tuning. The tallest bar, representing the “Sports” category before instruction tuning, has a value of 45.42%, while the shortest bar, representing “Healthcare” after instruction tuning, has a value of 0.11%.  Notably, the dark red bars are consistently positioned directly below their corresponding light gray bars, indicating a reduction in bias after instruction tuning.  The bars are not sorted in any particular order.
